note: Clean pass with one caveat: the paper's Methods says Sections II and III used a 5-point Likert scale 'from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree)', but the administered questionnaire (S1 File, Part II) prints '(A) very low (B) low (C) average (D) high (E) very high' for the AIC-CCS items. The questionnaire's anchors were shipped, because they are the instrument respondents actually saw and 'strongly disagree' is incoherent for stems like 'understanding native history'. A-E were mapped ascending to resp 1-5, consistent with the paper's own interpretive benchmark (mean <3.00 = low competence, >4.00 = extremely high) and its reported dimension means (AT 4.08, KN2 3.24).

Item text is the study's own deposit header row (pone.0340479.s002.xlsx, row 2), which labels every one of the 36 columns; item codes are assigned positionally by data/yang2026_efl_learner_perspective.py (cols 7-42 -> item_01..item_36) and the mapping was re-run and reproduced cell-for-cell against live data (5544/5544 cells, 154 ids). BLOCKED: no item wording published anywhere for the 14 administered items. The only supplement is S1 File (Data, .xlsx); its 3-row header carries a scale group ('ER'), a subscale code ('ER1' x7 cols 60-66, 'ER2' x7 cols 67-73) and a bare question number ('Q60'..'Q73') -- no item text in Chinese or English, and the article body has no item table (Tables 1-5 are construct-level CFA/correlation/mediation results). Instrument mismatch (Step 3b): the paper names the ERQ of Gross & John (2003), Chinese version adapted by Wang et al. (2007), but states 'The cognitive reappraisal dimension includes seven items' and 'The expressive suppression dimension also consists of seven items' -- 14 items, whereas both the original ERQ and the Wang et al. Chinese revision have 10 (6 reappraisal + 4 suppression). No 14-item ERQ version is known to exist, so canonical ERQ wording cannot be placed against item1..item14: there is no item-level correspondence to establish (the li_2024_sad shape). The data do confirm the 7/7 block structure and its direction -- items 1-7 intercorrelate 0.50-0.59 and correlate -0.19 to -0.25 with the RRS rumination mean, items 8-14 intercorrelate 0.48-0.58 and correlate +0.23 to +0.31 with it, matching the paper's SEM signs (reappraisal -0.359, suppression +0.449) -- so item1-7 = cognitive reappraisal and item8-14 = expressive suppression. That pins the subscales only; within each block the 7 items are statistically interchangeable (means 4.36-4.70, all r ~= 0.5), so even with wording in hand nothing would order them. Retry test: NO -- an unchanged retry cannot change this; the source never published the wording and the item count bars a canonical substitute. Flipping it needs the authors to release their questionnaire (Q60-Q73 wording), or a publication of the 14-item instrument with an explicit item-level correspondence to those question numbers. No rights bar was involved.
